title: fix(git.repo.test): a name:// scope on a journey frame fails for setup reasons and reads as a real break
description:
## .what
git.repo.test --scope name://X maps to jest --testNamePattern, which SKIPS every frame it does not match. in a journey test, frames are ordered and stateful: a later frame [tN] depends on setup an earlier frame left behind. run one later frame alone and it fails for setup reasons, and the output reads as a real break.

evidence (measured): a name-scoped run of one frame in a journey acceptance file reported 0 passed, 10 failed. the whole-file run of the same file reported 48 passed, 1 failed, and the one red was the clamp under test. the filter silently deleted the setup, then reported the consequence as a failure.

## .why
- a red suite demands action, so this is the wrong answer most likely to be acted on
- it lands hardest on a teeth proof (revert a fix, watch the clamp go red), whose whole job is to say whether one clamp bites
- the output is indistinguishable from a true break; nothing tells the caller the setup was skipped

## .shape of the fix
1. preferred: when a name:// scope resolves to a file that declares a journey (a .journey. filename, or [t0]..[tN] frame labels), warn at the invocation, e.g. "name:// filters frames out of a JOURNEY. its later frames depend on earlier ones, so a filtered run can fail for setup reasons. drop name:// to read this file honestly."
2. cheaper and weaker: a when/then row in howto.run-tests or rule.prefer.scoped-tests-locally
3. clamp: a fixture journey whose [t1] depends on [t0], run under --scope name://[t1]; assert the warn is emitted, and assert the naive failure count exceeds the whole-file run
